bluf: diva-e Conclusion is a German enterprise digital experience and transformation shop, now inside the Conclusion network, that builds platforms and attaches SEO, paid search and GAIO/GEO to them. The record shows it productising: an August 2026 marketplace of standardised digital services, an SAP partner grouping in May 2026, Google Premier Partner status for 2026. The Horus read rates it Favored at 14.5, best placed for the click giving way to the citation. A rival should know all 15 clients on record are names only, the deal with Conclusion has no shown date or type, and it sells AI visibility with no llms.txt of its own.
doing:
The positioning line reads: end to end digital experience and business transformation partner, strategy to operations, focused on B2B manufacturing, automotive, retail, pharma and financial services. In plain words: a platform builder and integrator for large German companies that also sells the marketing running on those platforms. The headline claim is rank, not results: market leader in DXS per the Lünendonk List 2025 and sixth in the BVDW agency ranking with Conclusion DACH.

The sold mix runs from consulting, UX, DXP, commerce, CDP, PIM and system integration to analytics, digital marketing, GAIO / GEO, cloud and diva-e AI. Web & Product is the sole lead line at 3 (the title bills a Digital Experience Partner; the Aumovio platform migration). Core lines at 2 are AI Automation / Agents (Agentic Experience Foundation, Product Advisor, Product Data Assistant, a private custom LLM), AI Search / GEO (a GAIO/GEO audit framework, guide downloads, 26 AI search URLs), Data & Measurement (Data Analytics & BI and CDP lines), Paid Search (a performance marketing audit page) and SEO (audit and relaunch pages, Powerpacks, the OneProSeo tool). Partners listed: Google Premier Partner (2026), Adobe, Storyblok and Crownpeak at Platinum, SAP through Conclusion, Salesforce.

The AI posture is build and audit: agentic AI foundations, AI product advisors, private custom LLMs and GAIO/GEO audits.

Moves in date order: the Lünendonk List 2025 kept it market leader; Google Premier Partner status came for 2026; in May 2026 it pooled SAP expertise with myBrand Conclusion and Score Conclusion; in August 2026 it launched a marketplace of productised services on reusable components. Undated: joining Conclusion and rebranding, and bringing Reventure under the diva-e umbrella. The pricing signal is the marketplace, pitched on predictability and lower project effort with no prices seen. Conspicuously absent for a commerce platform builder: paid social, programmatic and retail media all at 0, no jobs, no office list or own headcount.
clients:
The Radar files the client type as enterprise, the home market as Germany, and the verticals as B2B manufacturing, Automotive, Retail, Pharma & healthcare and Financial services. The needs read counts 15 clients and observes a need for none of them: 1 case study, 1 press release and 13 case study slugs, all named only, so the mix read is empty.

The names are heavy: Siemens, FC Bayern München, Postbank, SEAT, VWFS, Ravensburger, Klöckner & Co, GLS, SCHOTT, baby-walz, SMA, Puzzel Ltd and PFERD sit on client slugs, Interamt on a case study page, Aumovio in a press release. The one need the wider record describes is Aumovio, whose press release slug and the Web & Product capability note both describe a platform migration, which reads as web build and platform. Every other need is inferred from the sold mix: platform builds, systems integration and the SEO, paid search and GEO lines that run on them, and the sentence says so because no page on record describes the work.

One client is shared with other tracked agencies: Siemens also sits on the merkle and iprospect books. The whole book is names only (15 of 15), which for an agency claiming market leadership in DXS is the question to put to its clients.

What the base needs next: KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them) are its tailwinds, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that its manufacturing and automotive clients will be sold GAIO audits and product data assistants on top of platform retainers. It is a roughly even chance that the transition to the Conclusion brand loosens some of these accounts, since the record shows no deal date or type.
house: Say and do: 1 of 2 tested lines is practised on its own house. Publishing cadence is corroborated: 58 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 546 in 365, from a sitemap of 1,409 URLs, 26 of them AI search topics. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility, publishes GAIO guides and runs a GEO audit, yet has no llms.txt; no AI crawler is blocked. Paid search is unknown because the Transparency Center lookup was blocked. LinkedIn advertising is live: 15 company page ads (video, carousel, document) on platform choice and customer journeys, with a second pass finding 3 dynamic job and follower ads. One sample reads that 70% of digital transformations fail to meet their goals and that maybe technology is not the problem. The tag stack is GTM and Usercentrics on Nuxt with Storyblok; no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack are listed, a gap for a shop selling CDP work.

openings:
Lead with the empty book. Fifteen names and not one described case: a rival with written cases in manufacturing or automotive can ask what diva-e Conclusion did for Siemens or SEAT. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that the named slugs are logo pages rather than engagements a buyer can reference; the falsifier is a kunden page that describes scope and results.

Second, the say and do gap on AI search: 26 AI search URLs, a GAIO audit framework and no llms.txt, plus no feed, schema or entity work on record (P2 absent). A feeds and entities offer into its commerce clients undercuts the GAIO audit; very likely, high confidence.

Third, the transition: the Conclusion deal has no shown date or type and the brand carries two names; clients in a transition answer the phone, and Siemens, shared with merkle and iprospect, is the account to call first. Fourth, KJ6 exposure runs through paid search and SEO hours while its Transparency Center lookup is blocked, so a rival with visible paid results and ads tested inside AI assistants (P8 absent) sets the price; roughly even chance, low confidence, since marketplace pricing may already move those hours to fixed scope.
